content.content: An edit may be prepared as drafts before it is recorded into the graph. A draft names exactly one node — the node whose content it will change — and the edit it belongs to. An edit carries a draft for each node it touches; a node may carry several drafts — within one edit as competing alternatives, and across edits as a redraft while an earlier draft is still open. Each draft is written in its own workspace, so the drafts of one edit are written in parallel. A draft is not a graph node, and landing is per draft: each draft is recorded into its own node as its own operation, so an edit is a unit of review, never a unit of history.
content.rationale: A single piece of work usually decides several things at once, so the unit that is reviewed (an edit) and the unit that is placed (a node's change, D6) are different; the draft is the bridge between them. Counting drafts per draft — not per node — is what lets a node be redrafted while an earlier draft is open, and lets two drafts of one node compete in an edit. One workspace per draft is what makes parallel writing possible without two writers sharing a working copy. Landing per draft keeps D13's recording intact: one draft lands, one node's change grows.
